newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Slow budget approval forces Nigerian JVs to borrow.
newsitem.headline: Slow budget approval forces Nigerian JVs to borrow.

text.p: The failure of Nigeria's military government to approve a 1996 operating budget for foreign joint venture oil production partners has forced them to borrow to meet costs, a local newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The independent Guardian said the six largest joint venture partners had borrowed $300 million from banks abroad and 20 billion naira from Nigerian banks to pay staff and local contractors.
In June, halfway through the budget year, the government said it had cut the proposed 1996 budget of around $2 billion and 20 billion naira by around 30 percent.
However, industry sources are optimistic that a higher budget will eventually be approved.
There was no immediate comment from companies on the Guardian report.
Nigeria pumps around two million barrels of oil per day in joint ventures which are 55 to 60 percent owned by state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC).
The Shell joint venture accounts for about half of production. Other partners are Mobil, Chevron, Agip, Elf Aquitaine and Texaco.
